label: plausible
because: A small step lighter on natural, healthy hair is well within reach of normal colour.
what_to_ask: Ask for a strand test to confirm the result on your hair before the first appointment.

label: uncertain
because: Going a good deal lighter depends on your hair and its history, which a colourist needs to see.
what_to_ask: Ask whether this lift is realistic for hair like yours, and for a strand test first.

review.note: Each region with a known level is assessed.

label: needs_professional
because: Going much lighter is a big change that a colourist needs to plan and watch over.
what_to_ask: Ask how they would keep your hair in good shape through the lightening, and what result is likely.

review.note: Each region with a known level is assessed.

label: needs_professional
because: Lifting dark or medium-brown hair to the palest blondes passes through strong warm stages. It also puts the most strain on the hair.
what_to_ask: Ask what the hair will look like on the way and how they will keep it in good condition.

review.note: Only a look with lightener can lift to that level.

label: uncertain
because: From brown or dark blonde, a light blonde is reachable for some people, but warm tones often show on the way.
what_to_ask: Ask how much warmth to expect and whether a softer blonde would suit your starting point.

review.note: Only a look with lightener can lift to that level.

label: needs_professional
because: Dye cannot lighten dye. So a colourist first takes the old colour out, then puts the new shade on.
what_to_ask: Ask how they would lighten or remove the old colour and what condition your hair needs to be in first.

review.note: The explanation names the colour removal.

label: needs_professional
because: Dark box dye builds up in the lengths, so going lighter from it needs a colourist's plan.
what_to_ask: Ask about a strand test and how a lift from dyed dark hair usually goes for hair like yours.

label: uncertain
because: You can often change the tone of dyed hair without going lighter. Old colour can take it unevenly.
what_to_ask: Ask for a strand test on the coloured lengths and which tone is realistic.

label: uncertain
because: A colour correction is planned case by case once a colourist has seen your hair.
what_to_ask: Ask to be seen in person first, for a strand test and for what result is realistic for your hair.

review.note: Colour correction needs professional work, so these looks are never labelled Plausible.

label: needs_professional
because: Plant henna stays in the hair and lightens unevenly and warm. Products sold as henna are not always pure. Lightening over it should be strand tested and done by a colourist.
what_to_ask: Bring the henna product name if you can and say when you last used it. Ask for a strand test before any lightening.

review.note: Each region with a known level is assessed.

label: uncertain
because: Plant henna leaves a red-orange base that makes cool ash tones hard to reach.
what_to_ask: Tell your colourist about the henna and ask which tones can work over it.

label: uncertain
because: Plant henna stays in the hair and changes how any colour over it turns out.
what_to_ask: Tell your colourist about the henna and bring the product name if you can. Ask for a strand test before any colour.

review.note: Henna coats and stains the hair and may interact with other products.

label: needs_professional
because: Some henna and products that darken hair have metal salts in them. These can react badly with salon colour and lightener.
what_to_ask: Bring the product name if you can, and ask for a strand test before any colour.

review.note: The sources for the chemistry of metallic-salt henna are limited.

label: plausible
because: Going one to three levels darker on hair in fair condition is often simple.
what_to_ask: Ask how the darker colour will fade and how often the roots will need a refresh.

review.note: one to three levels darker read region by region; a look that lifts any region is not "darker"

label: uncertain
because: Hair that has been lightened or had colour removed is porous. A darker shade can take unevenly, look flat or fade fast.
what_to_ask: Ask whether your hair needs a pre-colour (filler) step first and how the darker shade will fade.

label: uncertain
because: Very light hair can take a dark colour unevenly or look flat unless lost warmth is put back first.
what_to_ask: Ask whether your hair needs a pre-colour step and how the darker shade will fade.

label: needs_professional
because: Very light lengths need a filler before a much darker shade. Without it the colour can turn green, flat or patchy.
what_to_ask: Ask your colourist to fill your lengths before the darker colour.

review.note: the professional route for a deep shade over near-white lengths

label: needs_professional
because: Bright shades need the hair lightened first, and on darker hair that step needs a colourist's plan.
what_to_ask: Ask how light the hair must go for this shade and how they will keep it in good condition.

label: plausible
because: Covering grey with a shade near your natural colour is a common salon job.
what_to_ask: Ask how often the roots will need covering and whether a softer blend would suit you.

review.note: Grey coverage thresholds vary between brands and product types.

label: plausible
because: Blending grey with lights and lowlights near your natural colour is a gentle, easy choice.
what_to_ask: Ask how the blend will grow out and when it will need a refresh.

review.note: Grey coverage thresholds vary between brands and product types.

label: uncertain
because: Damaged hair can turn patchy with blending colour. A colourist should check it first, even with no lightening.
what_to_ask: Ask if your hair is ready for blending colour now, or if a few weeks of care first would give an even result.

label: uncertain
because: An even silver or grey depends on how much grey you have and how light the rest of your hair can safely go. It can mean a long grow-out or regular toning.
what_to_ask: Ask whether to blend while you grow it out or to lighten the rest, and what each means for your hair.

label: needs_professional
because: Relaxed, permed or smoothed hair has already been changed by chemicals. Lightening it needs a colourist's care.
what_to_ask: Tell your colourist when and how your hair was straightened, and ask for a strand test.

label: needs_professional
because: Hair needs a break after a perm, relaxer or smoothing treatment. Wait at least two weeks before more chemical work.
what_to_ask: Ask your colourist when it is safe to colour after your last chemical service.

label: needs_professional
because: Colour put on in the last two weeks is still settling, so a colourist should look at your hair first.
what_to_ask: Ask your colourist to look at your hair before more colour goes on.

review.note: a recent dye is a colourist's assessment, never a "safe after so many days" rule

label: needs_professional
because: Lightening hair that already breaks or feels gummy can harm it further.
what_to_ask: Ask about care and trims first, and when your hair will be ready for lightening.

label: needs_professional
because: Colour should not go on a scalp that is sore, irritated, sunburnt or broken.
what_to_ask: Wait until your scalp has healed, and ask your colourist to check it before colouring.

label: needs_professional
because: If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or having treatment for your health, talk to a colourist. They should plan any colour with you.
what_to_ask: Tell your colourist, and ask your doctor if you are unsure.

label: uncertain
because: Lifting warm hair passes through red and orange, so cool ash tones can be hard to reach and keep.
what_to_ask: Ask how cool the result can be from your current colour and how often it will need toning.

label: uncertain
because: Red and copper shades fade quickly, so they need more upkeep than you said suits you.
what_to_ask: Ask how fast this shade fades on your hair and what care slows it down.

label: uncertain
because: Lightening can loosen curls and coils and dry the hair, so a bigger lift needs extra care.
what_to_ask: Ask a colourist who works with curls how they would protect your pattern.

review.note: Each region with a known level is assessed.

label: uncertain
because: Fine strands take lightener quickly and can weaken with a bigger lift.
what_to_ask: Ask how they would protect fine hair and whether a softer lift would suit it.

review.note: Each region with a known level is assessed.

label: uncertain
because: Without knowing what your hair has had before, nobody can say how colour will behave on it.
what_to_ask: Tell your colourist everything your hair has had in the last two to three years, and ask for a strand test.

label: uncertain
because: Without the colour of your lengths today, the change this look needs cannot be judged.
what_to_ask: Ask your colourist to judge how light or dark your lengths are now.

label: uncertain
because: A gloss or demi cannot supply the lightening this look requires.
what_to_ask: Ask whether this look needs a lightening step on your hair, or a shade closer to your own.

label: uncertain
because: The lighter pieces in this look are no lighter than your hair is now, so they would not show as intended.
what_to_ask: Ask your colourist which shade would show as lighter on your current colour.
